title: Ethiopian Flatbread
community: All of Ethiopia — the quick everyday unleavened flatbread
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Kita — a simple unleavened Ethiopian flatbread made from wheat flour and water, cooked on a dry pan. The quick-cooking, everyday alternative to injera — made in 25 minutes, used as a base for Chechebsa (Kita Firfir), or eaten with any stew.
longDesc: Kita is the quick bread of Ethiopian daily life — when there is no time for injera fermentation or no injera in the house, kita is made. Thicker than a tortilla and thinner than a pita, it is slightly chewy and neutral in flavour, serving as the perfect vehicle for the bold flavours of Ethiopian stews.
ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour or whole wheat flour
steps: Combine flour and salt. Add water gradually, mixing.
Knead 5 minutes until smooth. Add oil if using.
Divide into 4 balls. Roll each 3—4mm thick.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat: 3—4 minutes per side until cooked through and lightly browned.
chefTips: Kita should be thicker than a tortilla but thinner than a pita.
Cook over medium heat — high heat burns outside before inside cooks.
Keep wrapped in a cloth after cooking — they stay soft.
cookingScience: Unlike injera, kita has no fermentation — it is a simple starch-gluten system. The gluten network formed during kneading creates elasticity; without the acid of fermentation to partially break down this gluten, kita is slightly chewier and more dense than injera.
sustainabilityTips: The simplest possible bread — zero waste, minimal ingredients.
servedWith: With honey and butter for breakfast
reheating: Warm in dry pan or microwave.
culturalNote: Kita is the bread of practicality — made when time is short, when injera has run out, when the children are hungry. It is not a lesser bread but a different one — honest, direct, and perfectly functional.
